title: Slope from Slope-Intercept Form: Read the Rate, Not the Constant

scenes.title: In y = −x + 6, what is the slope?
body: Slope tells how y changes when x changes.
The equation is already in slope-intercept form.
Look at the coefficient attached to x.
scenes.narration: In y equals negative x plus six, what is the slope? A lot of students see the six and grab it because it is the obvious number. But here’s the idea: slope is not just a number sitting in the equation. Slope tells how much y changes when x increases. In slope-intercept form, the equation is arranged so that rate is visible immediately.

scenes.title: Why the x-coefficient is the slope
body: b is the value of y when x = 0.
scenes.substitution: Change x by 1 → mx changes by m.
scenes.narration: In y equals m x plus b, m multiplies x. That matters because if x increases by one, the term m x increases by exactly m, while b stays fixed. So y changes by m. Notice why that makes m the slope: it is literally the change in output for a one-unit change in input. The constant b has a different job. It tells you where the line starts on the y-axis when x is zero.

scenes.title: The sign students often lose
scenes.narration: This is where students often mix things up. In y equals negative x plus six, the coefficient is negative one, even though the one is not written. The negative sign belongs to the coefficient. So the slope is negative one. That means every time you move one unit to the right, the line moves one unit down. The six is the y-intercept, not the rate.

scenes.title: A fractional slope has the same meaning
scenes.narration: Now take y equals negative one-half x plus seven. The slope is negative one-half. Think of that as change in y over change in x: down one for every two units to the right. At x equals zero, y is seven. At x equals two, y is six. That movement is exactly what the coefficient negative one-half predicts.

scenes.title: Check the rate instead of memorizing
scenes.narration: Quick check: using the two points zero comma seven and two comma six, the change in y is negative one and the change in x is two, so the slope is negative one-half. The big idea is simple: in y equals m x plus b, m is the rate because it controls how y changes as x changes, while b is the starting value. Read the x-coefficient with its sign, including an implied one or negative one. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
